page0.text:
In the end, we got home before midnight.
We decided there wasn't any point in wasting our stamina when there was nothing else to do.

page1.text:
My feet feel heavy.
The physical stress of training all day must be catching up with me.
My body feels like lead, and my eyelids might droop closed at any moment.

page2.text:
...I'm sleepy.
Maybe my mind's worse off than my body.
I want to sleep so badly I might just curl up on the floor in this hallway.

page3.text:
"Welcome back. How did the town look, Rin?"
Illya was waiting for us in the living room.
...Sakura isn't here.
Of course not.
Sakura's...
"...Nrgh."
No.
Sakura should be sleeping in her room right now.

page4.text:
"We got there after it happened. How's Sakura?"
"Nothing happened to her. She's sleeping in bed, and it doesn't seem like she woke up. I think she's doing a little better thanks to the energy saved from not using Rider."

page5.text:
"Okay. Still, be careful. There's no telling when she might go out of control again."
It doesn't seem like Tohsaka's any worse off after seeing that ghost town.

page6.text:
"I'm tired, so I'm going to bed. What about you, Illya?"
"I'm going to rest too. We're going to forge it tomorrow, so I'd better get enough sleep so we don't fail."
Illya bids us good night and goes off to the tatami room.

page7.text: "That's it for today, then. Get some rest, Shirou. I don't think you've noticed, but you're really pale."

page8.text:
...My body feels heavy.
I do manage to roll out my futon even through my brain fog, thanks to daily muscle memory.

page9.text:
...
I collapse into bed.
When I roll onto my back and look up at the ceiling, I make a little time to think.

page10.text:
...
I try to think with my exhausted brain.

page11.text:
I think about my left arm.
About loosening the shroud today.
After experiencing unbearable agony and terror last night, I easily overcome it in a day.
It ended so easily, the pain and fear might well have never existed.
If I think seriously about what that means, I know the answer.

page12.text:
I think about Illya.
She told me that she couldn't live with me.
She said it would be nice, but that it couldn't happen.
Because she doesn't have long to live.
She told me something that anyone would know.

page14.text:
I think about Sakura.
Her life is becoming more confined with each passing day,
because the Crest Worms are feeding on her body and she doesn't have enough magical energy.
It isn't her fault.
It isn't Sakura's fault that her body is this way.
All I can do for her is share my magical energy.
If I give her some blood and supply her with enough power, she should hold together.

page15.text:
I close my eyes.
Illya said that we were all beyond saving.
There's only one choice to make.
I made it long ago.

page16.text:
"...Senpai? Are you back...?"
I hear a voice from the hallway.

page17.text:
"I'm awake. Come in, Sakura."
I get...up. Even if my...head isn't...working right, I wanted to see Sakura.

page18.text: "Pardon me. Sorry, I heard something, so I woke up... Um, I haven't said good night to you yet."

page19.text:
Sakura's her usual self.
She's introverted, thoughtful, and always holds in what she wants to say. But she's still the girl who tries to laugh and means so much to me.
Over the last year, she's become so stunningly beautiful that now I want to embrace her any time we're alone together. She's the person I promised to protect forever.

page20.text: "Um, that's all I wanted to say. I feel better thanks to you, and I think I'll sleep well tonight. I just wanted to let you know that you don't need to worry."

page21.text:
Sakura's her usual self.
Of course she is.
Why wouldn't she be?
She couldn't possibly be the Sakura that came onto me that one night.

page22.text:
"...Senpai? Um, am I disturbing you?
You look really sleepy, or rather, tired..."
"Sakura. Did you get a good sleep?"
"Hm?"
But I still voice my anxiety.
My tired mind can't organize its thoughts.

page23.text:
"Yes. It was a restful nap.
I still had scary dreams, but I managed to get through them because you stayed with me until I fell asleep."

page24.text:
Scary dreams.
I know I shouldn't ask what they were.
...
I say nothing, and reach for her long hair.

page25.text:
"Huh... Um, Senpai?"
"Come here, Sakura."
My hand falls from her hair to her shoulder, and I bring her in close.

page26.text:
"U-um, Senpai! I-I-I...!"
"You don't like it?"
I whisper into her ear as I hug her.

page27.text:
Sakura doesn't resist burying her head into my chest.
"...No. I'm so happy."
She lets herself relax and snuggles against me.

page28.text:
Then, I hug her very tightly.
I can't control myself.

page30.text:
"Guh...!"
I've always wanted to do this with her.
There's been so many times I wanted to hug Sakura until I pass out.
So I do.
Sakura's voice doesn't reach my brain.
All I hear is my ragged breathing.

page31.text:
It's Sakura who wants me, who needs me,
but before I know it, I'm the one who's being satisfied.
I lose track of time.
I try to keep watching this nightmare until morning, but the power soon goes out in my body.

page32.text:
I start to fall asleep, still holding Sakura's hand.
"Mm, mm... Senpai, I'm going to..."
Savoring her body heat through my hands, I fall into a deep sleep.

page33.text:
...Then, the rational part of me speaks.
My ecstatic brain recovers its calm in the abyss of sleep.

page34.text:
What will happen if you do this?
By drowning yourself in Sakura, maybe you're decisively admitting that your fears are justified.
